extension_description.message: Automatically sorts tabs that aren't in a group of your own into 9 groups (today, yesterday, … last year) by when they were opened or — an option in Settings — when they were last used, and moves them on after midnight. In Settings you can also add groups from bookmarks: tabs bookmarked in a chosen folder (optionally also any address on the bookmark's domain) get a group of their own. Automatic groups stay to the right of your own groups, from oldest to newest.

core_sandbox_mjs_without_module.message: $1 does not use import/export — by the extension convention its name should end with .js.

core_sandbox_es_module.message: $1 uses import/export — a classic script (.js) gets the SDK as sandboxSdk; a module with imports must be a JS module (.mjs).

core_sandbox_capability_denied.message: “$1”: the user did not allow this function to the module (Settings → Uploaded modules).

core_sandbox_capability_pending.message: “$1”: the function is waiting for the user's decision in Settings → Uploaded modules — until then it is refused.

core_sandbox_capability_forbidden.message: “$1” cannot be allowed to an uploaded module: $2

core_sandbox_capability_unknown.message: “$1”: the core does not offer such a function to uploaded modules.

core_sandbox_capability_block_page.message: the extension page belongs to the core — the module runs in another document, a DOM node cannot be passed in a message, a request is never synchronous and the module would see the data of the other modules.

core_sandbox_capability_block_gesture.message: the browser allows it only directly in the handler of a click — a request from the sandbox reaches the core as a message, not as a click (Firefox refuses it). For opening the popup, the sidebar and the floating window the core offers popup.open, sidebar.toggle and floatingWindow.toggle on a button it draws for the module (api.buttons).

core_sandbox_capability_block_extension.message: storage, messages and control of the whole extension — the module would get the data and settings of all modules, could act as another module or ask for permissions.

core_sandbox_capability_block_page_code.message: code and content of web pages — the module would run code on any page.

core_sandbox_capability_block_browser_da.message: private browser data (cookies of all sites, history, browsing data) — access to it cannot be narrowed down to what the module needs.

core_sandbox_capability_block_network.message: network rules and intercepting requests — they change or read the traffic of all pages.

core_sandbox_capability_bad_type.message: downloads.download: “$1” is not a content type (type/subtype).

core_sandbox_capability_about_floating_w.message: Open and close the extension's floating window on the current tab — only when you click the module's button. On first use the browser asks you for access to web pages.

core_sandbox_capability_about_sidebar_to.message: Open and close the extension's sidebar — only when you click the module's button.

core_sandbox_capability_about_popup_open.message: Open the extension's popup — only when you click the module's button.

core_sandbox_capability_about_storage_us.message: Find out how much the extension's own storages take up — only the number of items and the sizes (localStorage, the IndexedDB database of records, navigator.storage.estimate(), chrome.storage.local), never their content.
Learn that one of the extension's storages changed — which one (localStorage, the IndexedDB records, chrome.storage.local), never what changed.

core_sandbox_capability_about_build_sett.message: Read the build settings of the modules for their standalone extensions (modules/<module>/standalone.json — they are only in an extension run unpacked from the project folder) and whether the extension runs that way.

core_sandbox_capability_about_floating_w.message: Read the stored positions, sizes and state of the extension's floating window for all domains — that is, the list of the domains it was used on.
Change or delete the stored position, size and state of the floating window for single domains — the floating window then opens there accordingly. Every change is checked.
Get the stored positions, sizes and state of the floating window again after every change (e.g. when you move it on another tab).

core_sandbox_capability_about_pwa_info_l.message: Read the websites with an installable web app (PWA) the PWA Info module recorded while you browsed — their addresses, manifests and icons, the pages they appeared on, and when and how many times you visited them.

core_sandbox_capability_about_pwa_info_g.message: Find out whether the PWA Info module records new websites — whether it is in the module list, turned on and has recording turned on in its settings.

core_sandbox_capability_about_pwa_info_o.message: Be told right away when the PWA Info module records or completes a website (on any tab — that is, when you visit a website with an app) or when its settings change.

core_sandbox_capability_about_domain_inf.message: Read the domains of the page in the current tab as the Domain Info module knows them — which of them the page used and how, the data it loaded about them from RDAP servers (holders and contacts with names, addresses, e-mails and phones, registrars, dates, name servers) with its history, and the paused servers; only the domains of that page.

Have the Domain Info module load the domains of the page in the current tab from RDAP servers right now (the “Load data from RDAP” button) — it sends the domain names to the RDAP servers set in its settings, within their limits.
End the pause of an RDAP server from the settings of the Domain Info module that did not respond, so that it is asked again right away (the “Retry now” button).

Turn saving data of the Domain Info module on or off (the same setting as in Settings) — while on, it makes no request to the RDAP servers by itself and loads only when you ask (the “Load data from RDAP” button).

Be told right away when the Domain Info module stores data about a domain of the page shown (on any tab), when the page in the current tab uses another domain or another tab is switched to, or when its settings change.

Read everything the Domain Info module recorded — the data it loaded from RDAP servers about all domains (holders and contacts with names, addresses, e-mails and phones, registrars, dates, name servers) with their history, the pages the domains were found on, the stored copies of contacts and the failed loads; not only the domains of one page.

core_sandbox_capability_about_image_info.message: Read the images of the page in the current tab as the Image Info module lists them — their addresses, where and how the page uses them, how they loaded, their HTTP response headers and the metadata of their files (cameras, dates, GPS positions, authors, descriptions); only the images of that page.

Download an image of the page in the current tab once more (the “Load information” button) and read its HTTP response headers and the metadata of its file — when the page loaded it before the recording or the browser does not keep its file; only the images the listing of that page shows. The image is transferred from its server again.

Read the file of an image of the page in the current tab to show its thumbnail in the listing — from what the browser already has (its cache, a data: or blob: address), or with the button "Show" downloaded from its server once more (its HTTP headers and metadata are kept too); only the images the listing of that page shows.

Save an image of the page in the current tab as a download (the button "Save image" / "Download") — from what the browser already has (its cache, a data: or blob: address), otherwise downloaded from its server once more; only the images the listing of that page shows.

Remove an image of the page in the current tab from that page (the button “Remove from the document”): its elements go away, an image from CSS is turned off — the page stays so until it is reloaded; only the images the listing of that page shows.

Block an image of the listing permanently (the button “Block the image permanently”): its address goes into the rule “Image info sandbox - blocked images” of the Declarative Net Request module — the browser then does not load it on any page until the address is removed from the rule in Settings; only the images the listing of the page shows.

Show marks over the images of the page in the current tab, on that page itself (the columns “Show on the page” and “Show on the page over larger images” of the notices): a badge with icons over an image and short texts under the mouse pointer with the name of the module — only the images the listing of that page shows, and only while the listing is open.
Be told right away when the page in the current tab loads more images, or when the settings of the Image Info module, the module list or the permissions change.

Know which images of the page in the current tab are visible right now and which one is under the mouse pointer (or was tapped) — the Image Info module follows the scrolling and the pointer on that page while the listing is open.

core_sandbox_capability_about_studies_ma.message: Read the scientific studies the Studies Manager module recorded on the pages you browsed — their identifiers (DOI, PubMed, arXiv), titles, authors, journals, abstracts and other metadata, and the pages they appeared on (their addresses and titles — a part of your browsing history), with when and how many times.
Find out whether the Studies Manager module records new studies — whether it is in the module list, turned on and has recording turned on in its settings.
Be told right away when the Studies Manager module records or completes studies (on any tab — that is, when you visit a page with a study) or when its settings change.
Have the Studies Manager module load the metadata of the chosen studies from doi.org right now — their DOIs are sent to doi.org and to the registry of each DOI (Crossref, DataCite, …).
Remove studies recorded by the Studies Manager module — they disappear from the list until you come across them again.

core_sandbox_capability_about_contacts_m.message: Read the contacts the Contacts Module module recorded on the pages you browsed — the names, e-mails, phones, addresses and other details of people and organizations, and the pages they appeared on (their addresses and titles — a part of the browsing history), when and how many times.
Find out whether the Contacts Module module records new contacts — whether it is in the module list, turned on and has recording turned on in its settings.
Be told right away when the Contacts Module module records contacts (on any tab — that is, when you visit a page with a business card) or when its settings change.
Remove contacts recorded by the Contacts Module module — they disappear from the list until you come across them again.
Change the details of contacts recorded by the Contacts Module module (name, e-mails, phones, web addresses, …) and their tags — your changes are shown instead of the details found on the pages.

Load the public record of an ORCID iD of a contact recorded by the Contacts Module module (pub.orcid.org learns which iD is asked about) and add its details (name, other names, biography, web addresses, e-mails, employment, …) to the contact.

Load the whole public Gravatar profile of a contact recorded by the Contacts Module module (gravatar.com learns which profile is asked about) and add its details (name, bio, web addresses, e-mails, phones, job, verified accounts, …) to the contact.

Load the whole account of a profile on the fediverse (Mastodon) of a contact recorded by the Contacts Module module from its instance (the server of the address learns which account is asked about) and add its details (name, bio, picture, web addresses and e-mails of the fields, verified links, …) to the contact.

Load a Keyoxide profile of a contact recorded by the Contacts Module module from keyoxide.org (it learns which profile is asked about, fetches its key and verifies its claims) and add its details (name, description, picture, e-mails, key, verified accounts and domains) to the contact.

Merge two contacts recorded by the Contacts Module module into one — the older contact gets the pages, the details and the linked accounts of the newer one (where they differ, the values you choose) and the newer one is removed.
Import contacts into the Contacts Module module — the contacts of a file you choose in the manager (a vCard or the CSV of its export) are joined with the recorded contacts or stored as new ones.
Turn saving data of the Contacts Module module on or off (the same setting as in Settings) — while on, it takes the contacts only from the open pages and downloads nothing more itself.

core_sandbox_capability_about_service_wo.message: lists the service workers Service Worker Control finds — the websites with a service worker in open tabs (with the “debugger” permission also all running ones) and those seen earlier, with the titles of their pages and their icons
stops a running service worker of the overview (Chrome briefly attaches the debugger to it)
starts a stopped service worker of the overview through an open page of its website
unregisters service workers of the overview — the websites register them again on the next visit unless their domain is blocked
blocks the domain of a website of the overview — it is added to the list of Service Worker Control in Settings, its pages then have no Service Worker API and its service workers are unregistered
forgets a remembered website of the overview — its record of Service Worker Control is removed
learns when a service worker of the overview stops or starts, when the records of the websites change (an icon was downloaded) and when the settings or permissions of Service Worker Control change

core_sandbox_capability_about_tab_groups.message: lists the automatic tab groups Tab Groups manages in the current window — their names, colors and numbers of tabs, how many groups of your own and unsorted tabs there are — how tabs are sorted and which permissions of Tab Groups are missing (not the addresses or titles of the tabs)
has Tab Groups sort the tabs of all windows into its groups right now
makes the groups Tab Groups manages briefly blink in all windows
reads the settings of Tab Groups — how tabs are sorted, the names and colors of the groups, the groups from bookmarks with the names of the bookmark folders (with the permission to bookmarks)
changes the settings of Tab Groups (Tab Groups checks every value the same way as in Settings)
opens the page where Tab Groups asks for its permissions
learns when a tab group or a tab of the window changes and when the settings or permissions of Tab Groups change

core_sandbox_capability_about_declarativ.message: reads which rules of Declarative Net Request target the page of the active tab and what they do (headers, GET parameters, blocking), which of them are suspended and how the rules turned out in the browser

reads all rules of Declarative Net Request — the domains, addresses and bookmark folders they target, the headers and parameters they set — with the names of the bookmark folders (with the permission to bookmarks), the granted permissions and the suspended rules

replaces the rules of Declarative Net Request (it checks every rule the same way as in Settings) — the browser then changes the headers and GET parameters of requests and blocks requests by them on all pages
suspends a rule of Declarative Net Request for an hour — the browser does not apply it until then
ends the suspension of a rule of Declarative Net Request — the browser applies it again
reloads the page of the active tab of the window, so that the rules of Declarative Net Request apply to all its requests

reads the own event log of Declarative Net Request — the requests its rules with the event log were applied to on all pages: the addresses of the requests and of the pages they came from, the tabs and the times
deletes an entry of the own event log of Declarative Net Request, or the whole log

learns when the rules or the settings of Declarative Net Request change, when a rule is suspended or restored, when its event log changes, when the module list or the permissions change and when the bookmarks change

core_sandbox_capability_about_content_fi.message: Inject uBlock Origin scriptlets and hide elements on the pages of the hosts the module names (only those it asks the access to) by the rules of the filter lists it names — the extension downloads the lists from those addresses (https) and keeps them up to date, also when the module is not shown. The module brings no code for the pages, but the “trusted-…” scriptlets of a list it marks as trusted can change any text or code of those pages. It can also mark the tab icon of the pages the rules run in.
Read the state of its content filters — how they are injected into pages (or why not), the filter lists with the date of the download and the number of rules, what was built of them.
Have the filter lists of its content filters downloaded again right now (otherwise they are downloaded after they expire).
Be told right away when its content filters change (a list downloaded, the rules built again, another way of injecting) or when its settings change.

core_sandbox_capability_about_network_fi.message: Block requests on all pages by the network rules of the filter lists the module names — the extension downloads the lists from those addresses (https) and keeps them up to date, also when the module is not shown, and converts them into declarativeNetRequest blocking rules itself. The module gives no rules, only the lists, so it cannot redirect or change a request — but a list can block any page or anything it loads. Only for a module that declares the permissions to block requests on all pages.

Read the state of its network filters — how many of its rules apply in the browser (or why none), the filter lists with the date of the download and the number of rules, what could not be converted, the domains on which nothing is blocked.
Have the filter lists of its network filters downloaded again right now (otherwise they are downloaded after they expire).
Be told right away when its network filters change (a list downloaded, the rules converted again) or when its settings change.

core_sandbox_capability_about_scheduled_.message: lists your devices with this extension (their names, browsers and systems, when they were last in use) and the addresses scheduled for them, including the history of the opened ones — the browser carries them between the devices of your account (Chrome sync, Firefox Sync)
schedules an address for your devices — the extension opens it on each of them at the given time in a new tab in the background, also while the module is not shown
renames one of your devices in the list
forgets another of your devices and the addresses scheduled for it
has the extension open the addresses of this device whose time has come right now

pairs the module with VS Code on this computer (the plugin of this extension for VS Code) — the extension then copies your devices and scheduled addresses between the browser and VS Code, whose Settings Sync carries them to your other VS Code instances; it reaches the plugin only at the address 127.0.0.1
cancels the pairing with VS Code on this computer
learns when the devices or the scheduled addresses change, also on another device

core_sandbox_capability_about_dns_overvi.message: Read the hosts the page in the current tab contacted, as the extension follows its requests — the addresses of the servers, the responses from the HTTP cache, the names that were not resolved, in Firefox also what the browser's DNS cache holds for them and whether the connections used encrypted DNS — with the answers of the DNS queries loaded for them; only the hosts of that page. Denying it stops the following of the pages.

Have the extension ask the DNS about hosts of the page in the current tab right now (the button “🔄”) — past the browser's cache, and over the system resolver too when the browser uses DNS over HTTPS (Firefox); only the hosts the page contacted. Denying it also stops the automatic loading with the probability set at the module.
Learn right away when the page in the current tab contacts another host or new DNS data of its hosts come, and when what the extension can do changes (settings, permissions).

core_sandbox_problem_not_sandboxed.message: The sandbox page is not isolated (it does not have an opaque origin) — the module code was not run.

core_sandbox_problem_eval_blocked.message: The browser does not allow running code in the sandbox page — uploaded modules need sandboxed extension pages (Chrome, Firefox 154 or newer).

core_sandbox_problem_no_registration.message: The module did not call registerModule() while it was evaluated.

core_sandbox_problem_multiple_registrati.message: The module called registerModule() more than once.

core_sandbox_problem_not_object.message: registerModule() did not get an object.

core_sandbox_problem_name_mismatch.message: registerModule({ name: "$1" }) — the name must be the same as the file name: "$2".

core_sandbox_problem_tag_mismatch.message: registerModule({ tag: "$1" }) — the tag must be getTagName(name): "$2".

core_sandbox_problem_not_defined.message: The element <$1> is not defined with customElements.define() before registerModule().

core_sandbox_problem_not_base_element.message: The class of the element <$1> does not inherit from BaseElement of the sandbox SDK.

core_sandbox_problem_unsupported.message: registerModule({ $1 }) is not available to uploaded modules (it would be code outside the sandbox).

core_sandbox_problem_custom_field.message: The settings field “$1” has the type “custom” — uploaded modules have text, textarea, number, checkbox and select fields only.

core_sandbox_problem_not_data.message: registerModule({ $1 }) must contain data only (JSON) — no functions or class objects.

core_sandbox_problem_bad_spec.message: activationSpec must be built from the specifications of sandboxSdk (ModeSpecification, WEB_PAGE_SPEC, …) with valid values.

core_sandbox_problem_bad_style.message: registerModule({ styles }) — “$1” is not a CSS file of the module package.

core_sandbox_problem_unknown.message: The sandbox reported an unknown problem.

options_modules_json_hint_disable.message: The easier way to turn a module off is “Advanced module settings” → “Module activation mode” → “Never start (module inactive)”. The module stays in its place in the list and you turn it back on with a single switch.

options_modules_json_hint_performance.message: Removing it from the list saves more performance, though: the content script of a turned-off module is still inserted into every page (and only there finds out it has nothing to do), and the side panel, the floating window and Settings still load its file. A module that is not in the list is not loaded at all. The difference shows mainly with modules that work in pages.

options_unsaved_changes.message: Do not forget to save the changes you made

options_hint_not_displayed.message: Nothing is ticked, so the module is not shown anywhere. Depending on its activation mode it may still work in the background.

options_hint_disabled.message: The module is turned off (activation mode “Never start”), so it is not shown anywhere.

options_sidebar_disabled.message: Do not use the side panel

options_sidebar_disabled_hint_firefox.message: Modules are not shown in the side panel, which shows only a notice instead (an open panel closes). Firefox does not let an extension hide its icon in the sidebar launcher, so remove it yourself: right-click the icon and choose to remove it from the sidebar (Firefox 143 and newer). You can bring it back when customizing the sidebar. The ticked “In the side panel” locations of modules stay stored for when you turn the panel on again.

options_sidebar_disabled_hint_chrome.message: Modules are not shown in the side panel, and the extension's panel disappears from the browser's side panel menu. The ticked “In the side panel” locations of modules stay stored for when you turn the panel on again.

options_sidebar_disabled_saved.message: The side panel is turned off.

options_sidebar_enabled_saved.message: The side panel is turned on.

options_location_sidebar_off.message: The side panel is turned off (“Do not use the side panel” at the top of the page).

options_hint_sidebar_only.message: Only the side panel is ticked and it is turned off, so the module is not shown anywhere. Depending on its activation mode it may still work in the background.

options_sandbox_hint.message: A module uploaded from a file runs in an isolated page (sandbox) without access to the extension — it asks the extension core for everything else (its settings, stored data, the current tab, …). Otherwise it is a module like the others: in the module list, with an activation mode, output locations and its own settings. Upload one script named after the module (<name>.js, or <name>.mjs as a JS module), or a .zip with the module folder — more JS modules, CSS, images and texts (messages.json). Samples are in sandbox-modules/ in the extension repository.

options_services_hint.message: This extension can offer its modules to the full AnalyticExtension when it is installed: once you allow it in the Settings of AnalyticExtension, it shows them in its popup, side panel and Settings, but this extension keeps doing the work for them with its own permissions and settings. It is an export from here only — modules of other extensions cannot be added to this extension.
